clues: This coal town sits just north of the Arctic Circle in Russia. It lies in a coal basin by a river.
This town holds the cold record for the whole of Europe. Its coldest weather hit fifty two degrees below zero.
After the Soviet Union fell, its mines were sold off. Many people left and moved farther south.
Many of its coal mines now stand empty, left behind for good. The pits that once drove the town sit silent.
This is the farthest east town in all of Europe. It is one of the five biggest towns past the Arctic Circle.
